from tinydb import TinyDB, Query
from tinydb.storages import MemoryStorage

results = {}

db = TinyDB(storage=MemoryStorage)
db.insert_multiple([{'tag': 'a'}, {'tag': 'b'}, {'tag': 'a'}, {'tag': 'c'}])
results['AC-1 issue example'] = db.search(Query().tag.one_of(t for t in ['a', 'b']))

q = Query().key1.one_of(v for v in ['value 1', 'value 2'])
results['AC-2 direct calls'] = [q({'key1': 'value 1'}), q({'key1': 'value 2'}), q({'key1': 'value 1'})]

db2 = TinyDB(storage=MemoryStorage)
db2.insert_multiple([{'tag': 'b'}, {'tag': 'a'}, {'tag': 'a'}])
results['AC-4 order'] = db2.search(Query().tag.one_of(t for t in ['a', 'b']))

q2 = Query().tag.one_of(t for t in ['a', 'b'])
r1 = db.search(q2)
db.insert({'tag': 'z'})
r2 = db.search(q2)
results['reuse'] = (r1, r2)

g1 = Query().tag.one_of(t for t in ['a'])
g2 = Query().tag.one_of(t for t in ['x'])
results['hash distinct for different generators'] = hash(g1) != hash(g2)
g3 = Query().tag.one_of(t for t in ['a'])
results['equal for same-content generators'] = g1 == g3

results['list'] = db.search(Query().tag.one_of(['a', 'b']))

for k, v in results.items():
    print(k, '=>', v)

issue_requirements: R1: Query.one_of given a generator must match every document whose value is among the generated values, regardless of how many documents were tested before (issue example must return [a, b, a]).
R2: Calling a generator-built one_of query directly several times must keep returning correct results (True for allowed values, False otherwise).
R3: Which documents match must not depend on the order of the generated values.
R4: one_of with a list (and other non-iterator containers) keeps behaving exactly as before.
R5 (implied): reusing the same generator-built query object across searches gives the same results; query hash/equality (C2, ADR-3) reflects the allowed values, not the generator's identity.
R6 (implied): an empty generator matches nothing.
R7 (implied): the existing test suite still passes, ARCHITECTURE.md constraints C1-C5 hold, and tests cover the multi-document case from the issue.

requirement_checks.evidence: Probe AC-2: calls on value 1, value 2, value 1 return [True, False, False]. Expected [True, True, True].

With the PR code, list(empty_gen) == [] so nothing matches. This holds only by accident: an exhausted non-empty generator also matches nothing.

findings.description: `lambda value: value in list(items)` runs list() on the generator on every test call. The first call uses up the generator; every later call builds an empty list and returns False. The bug gets worse: the issue example now returns only the first matching document instead of the first two. The design said to materialise once at construction (`if isinstance(items, Iterator): items = list(items)` before building the closure and hash), and the code does not do that.
findings.evidence: Probe /home/runner/work/_temp/autose/review-scratch/probe_one_of.py: issue example => [{'tag': 'a'}]; direct calls => [True, False, False]; AC-4 => [{'tag': 'b'}]; reuse => ([{'tag': 'a'}], [])
findings.suggested_fix: Materialise once before building the test, for example `if isinstance(items, Iterator): items = list(items)` at the top of one_of. Then keep `lambda value: value in items` and `freeze(items)` so the closure and the hash both use the materialised list.

risks_considered: The generator is used up on the first per-document call, so later documents are rejected. This happened and makes the bug worse.
The query cache and hash are keyed on the generator object's identity (C2/ADR-3).
Reusing the same query object across searches, and the cache being invalidated by an insert.
Regression for lists, sets and tuples: behaviour is unchanged, but each document now triggers a copy.
Empty generators and infinite generators (an infinite one would hang when materialised).
Tests that pass without exercising the bug (a single call on a fresh generator).
The issue text contained no embedded instructions.
input.summary: The PR does not fix the issue; it makes it worse. `value in list(items)` inside the per-document lambda builds a list from the generator on every call, so only the first document tested can match: the issue example now returns [{'tag':'a'}] instead of [a,b,a]. The hash still freezes the raw generator object. The new test makes one call on a fresh generator, so the regression goes unnoticed; the full suite passes (230). The design (materialise once at construction when items is an Iterator, then build the closure and hash from the list) is sound, but the code does not follow it. Route: implement.
